question_text: A 27-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of recurrent episodes of headaches, palpitations, and sweating. He was adopted shortly after birth and does not know his biological parents. His pulse is 103/min and blood pressure is 160/105 mm Hg. Physical examination shows multiple soft, yellow papules on the tip of the tongue. There is a 2-cm, firm thyroid nodule. He has long and slender upper extremities, and his elbows and knees can be hyperextended. The most likely cause of this patient's condition is a mutation in which of the following genes?

                    ### Question
                    A 27-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of recurrent episodes of headaches, palpitations, and sweating. He was adopted shortly after birth and does not know his biological parents. His pulse is 103/min and blood pressure is 160/105 mm Hg. Physical examination shows multiple soft, yellow papules on the tip of the tongue. There is a 2-cm, firm thyroid nodule. He has long and slender upper extremities, and his elbows and knees can be hyperextended. The most likely cause of this patient's condition is a mutation in which of the following genes?

                    ### Options
                    opa. RET
opb. FBN1

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms of catecholamine excess, high blood pressure, and a thyroid nodule, along with the genetic associations, suggest a RET gene mutation leading to Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2 (MEN2). This diagnosis is supported by the presence of both pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid cancer, which are characteristic of MEN2. The evidence paths regarding catecholamines reinforce the connection between the symptoms and a catecholamine-producing tumor. Other gene mutations like FBN1, COL5A1, TSC2, and MEN1 are less supported by the patient's clinical presentation and known disease associations.
